threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to queue at the post office, instead of just chatting with the cashier like it’s your local pub.
Last night on the 59, a lad serenaded us all with a karaoke version of 'Wonderwall'—his girlfriend recorded it. The whole bus clapped at the end.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a neighbor grilling kebabs on their balcony while their cat chased pigeons below. Welcome to Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can buy a schnitzel from a food truck at 2 AM after a night out, and it’ll be the best thing you’ve ever eaten at that hour.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell they're local if they still call it 'the 16' instead of '16th Street.' Only tourists number their buses.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, I saw a guy serenading the 19 bus passengers with a ukulele. Everyone was smiling despite the usual delays. Only in SF!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the plaça is just for pictures, but locals use it to catch up and share a quick vermut with friends, everyday.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order their coffee—still asking for 'un café' instead of knowing it's just 'café' here.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think you can catch the Tube after 10pm without a struggle. Good luck with that during the strikes, mate.
Caught a night bus home from Brixton last week, saw a group of lads arguing over who had the best chicken shop. Classic South London.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I spotted the regulars at the 24/7 Späti arguing over the best Döner in the hood. The passion is real.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM that sells gourmet options like truffle sauce—classic Berlin meets high-end twist.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows the secret of squeezing past the bus stop crowd at 16th and Mission without breaking stride—even when the BART's down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 49 last week, packed with tourists trying to figure out how to pronounce 'Civic Center.' Classic San Francisco confusion.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just walk into any bar and get a great meal. Most locals know to check the daily menú del dia first.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still scan the menu for a good ten minutes, lost on the local dishes, while the waiters look on with patience.
